name: tractor
source: Geometry (wheelbase 2.80 m, track 1.90 m, front wheel radius 0.8 m, rear wheel radius 1.025 m) matches data/models/tractor/tractor.rig.json. Mass (6000 kg) and a rear-heavy 35/65 front/rear static split are plausible for a mid-size 2WD row-crop tractor per Wong, 'Theory of Ground Vehicles', 5th ed., ch. 1-2 - not a specific measured machine. Rigid axles are approximated by very stiff, short-travel per-wheel springs (PLAN.md 5.1's rigid/pendulum axle model is deferred). Front tyres data/tyres/tractor_front.json, rear data/tyres/tractor_rear.json. Powertrain (PHYS-033 I3): data/engines/diesel_i4_4l5_turbo.json -> dry clutch -> data/gearboxes/tractor_12f4r.json -> transfer case -> open rear differential with final drive 20.0 (bevel ~4.1 x planetary final ~4.9, typical tractor range) -> RL/RR; replaces the P3 placeholder's single final_drive_ratio = 15.0. Clutch 900 N*m kinetic (~1.55 x engine peak), static factor 1.2. Aero drag_area 4.0 m^2 (Cd ~0.8 x ~5 m^2 frontal area; minor at tractor speeds). Rear attachment z = -0.275 (PHYS-033 I1 fix, kept as-is per I3 plan section 10.2's own note - see the pre-I3 revision of this file for the derivation): matches the front's ground-contact offset exactly, not the -0.725 a level reproduction from I2 HEAD alone would suggest. PHYS-033 P4 I4 C9 (MFWD, mechanical front-wheel drive, default OFF via the 'awd' control channel defaulting to 0): a 'transfer' transfer_case component sits between gearbox.out and the rear differential's carrier (transfer.in <- gearbox.out, transfer.rear -> diff.carrier, unchanged ratio/efficiency), with a new 'front_diff' open differential (transfer.front -> front_diff.carrier -> FL/FR) providing a standard tractor MFWD ~2% front-axle speed lead: front_diff.ratio = 15.30 = (diff.ratio * r_F) / (transfer.front_ratio * r_R) = (20.0 * 0.8) / (1.0 * 1.025) / 1.02 (r_F/r_R = front/rear rolling radius 0.8/1.025 m, transfer.front_ratio = 1.0 pure passthrough, the whole lead realized via the front diff's own ratio vs. the rear diff's 20.0) - lead check: (20.0*0.8)/(15.30*1.025) = 1.0202, i.e. 2.02% front lead, matching the class-typical 1-3% MFWD lead that keeps the front axle in light drive (never overrunning the rear) on a straight line. front_diff carrier inertia 0.2 kg*m^2 (lighter duty than the rear diff's 0.5 - the front axle differential on a 2WD-converted tractor is a smaller unit). Transfer case clutch capacity_nm 2500 N*m, static_factor 1.2, engage_time_s 0.3 s - plausible for a hydraulically-actuated multi-plate MFWD clutch pack on this class of tractor, deliberately well under the driveline's own peak torque (engine 580 N*m x gearbox 1st-gear ratio 21.0 x 0.95 efficiency ~ 11.6 kN*m at gearbox.out) so the clutch slips rather than shock-loading the front axle when engaged at a large front/rear speed mismatch (e.g. a tight turn). test_powertrain_mfwd.cpp (tests/validation) is this component's acceptance test. PHYS-033 P4 I4 C10 (park lock, owner ruling): a 'park' park_lock component shares the same shaft as gearbox.out/transfer.in (the shafts[] entry now lists three ports) - a park pawl physically clamps the gearbox output shaft, upstream of the transfer case and both differentials, so it holds every wheel through whichever axle(s) MFWD currently connects. capacity_nm 30000 N*m (~2.6x the driveline's own peak torque at gearbox.out computed above, matching a real pawl's large mechanical-advantage margin over the torque it is designed to react, not to slip under), static_factor 1.0 (a pawl tooth engaged in a ring gear has no separate static/kinetic friction regime the way a clutch plate does - it either holds or it shears), max_engage_speed_rad_s 5.0 rad/s at gearbox.out (a plausible walking-pace shaft speed below which a dog-style pawl can find a tooth to drop into), channel "park_lock" (declared via Powertrain::declare_control_channels, default 0 = released). With MFWD off (the default) the pawl reaches the wheels through the open rear differential only. Measured (test_vehicle_tractor_cross_slope.cpp): park_lock alone in neutral holds 15% longitudinal to 1.4e-4 m over 30 s (the same rig with park_lock = 0 rolls 520 m); park_lock plus handbrake on the 10% cross slope drifts 4.5e-6 m. PHYS-033 P4 I4 C11 (power take-off): a 'pto' component sits on the engine crank shaft (pto.in shafted with engine.crank/clutch.in, live whenever the engine turns, ahead of the main clutch) with the two standard PTO speeds defined by ASAE/SAE S203 (540 and 1000 rpm); ratios 3.61 and 1.95 both reach their nominal PTO speed at ~1950 crank rpm (540*3.61 = 1949.4, 1000*1.95 = 1950), below the engine's 2200 rpm rated speed (data/engines/diesel_i4_4l5_turbo.json). Measured (tests/validation/test_powertrain_pto.cpp, viscous dyno c = 5 N*m*s/rad): engine/pto speed ratio exact to 1e-9 in both modes, clutch slip ~5e-12 rad/s. capacity_nm 700 N*m and efficiency 0.96 are plausible for a mid-size tractor's PTO gear train (a few percent mesh loss); static_factor 1.2 and engage_time_s 1.5 s mirror the transfer case's own clutch parameters above (a comparable wet multi-plate PTO clutch); out_inertia_kgm2 0.05 kg*m^2 is the bare PTO shaft/stub only (no implement attached in any shipped scenario); disengaged_brake_time_s 1.0 s is an engineering choice (not measured), the coordinator's own decay time constant for the otherwise-undamped disengaged PTO shaft (plan section 3.5's own gap - nothing else in the model dissipates its energy once nothing is connected to it). The all-speed governor still arrives in a later increment. PHYS-033 P4 I4 C15: the rear differential ('diff') is now lockable (channel 'diff_lock', default 0 = open, max_engage_mismatch_rad_s 2.0 matching this codebase's other lockable-diff defaults) - a real row-crop tractor diff lock for straight-line traction in soft/uneven field conditions; with diff_lock left at 0 the physics is unchanged (Differential::ReconMode switches from Leaf to LeafPair, which is mathematically exact for an unlocked open diff - components.h's own comment), but the reconstructed lambda_mesh_prev_ this lossy diff hashes is computed via a different summation (reconstruct_mesh_torque_pair, not reconstruct_mesh_torque) and is therefore not bit-identical to the pre-C15 value - measured: every pre-C15 tractor test's own state_hash VALUE changed, while the property each test actually asserts (1-vs-10-worker hash equality; no test pins a literal tractor hash) is confirmed unaffected, and every pre-C15 tractor test still passes.
